gravity_note: These tests were in microgravity on the ISS. The Moon is about one-sixth Earth's gravity. Pressure was recorded only for the 5 Saffire IV/V tests (70.7–100.0 kPa); the BASS-II tables give none, so a Moon-base condition is not covered by these tests.
gravity_note_short: These tests were in microgravity on the ISS. The Moon is about one-sixth Earth's gravity, and pressure differs, so a Moon-base condition is not covered by these tests.
rules: A test whose flow changed covers its whole span, from start to end flow.
NEAR means just outside the tested range: 1.0 oxygen point, or 25% of the material's flow range.
Fewer than 3 tests for a material means extrapolated, not covered.
Flows under 2 cm/s are flagged as uncertain (team choice: the BASS-II report says low flows have high error bars but gives no number).
If the crew turned the flow off and the flame went out, the outcome is unknown, not quenched.
Saffire V tests (about 71 kPa) are kept out of the standard ranges and shown by pressure.
Link et al. 2018 rows are paper rod data: not outcome evidence, different flow calibration.
Outcomes that are not recorded are shown as unknown, never guessed.
ranking_note: Scored by Lane B (Paridhi Singh), Nov 14, 2026. This ranking is the team's judgement, not NASA's. Fire-safety +3 goes to any sub-area mentioning 'fire', plus all three Saffire experiments (PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-100) as one NASA project — a team call, not NASA's.
